text:
Rafael Mendes: starting prod controlled failover window for low-risk slice (per plan). Scope: Hosted API only, route `/v1/chat.completions`, tier=dev+startup, canary cap 1% -> 10% max. Target region: us-west -> us-east. If anything feels off we abort fast. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.dev/runbooks/automated-region-failover (section: Controlled prod test)

incident-bot: Incident channel created for controlled failover test. Commander: Rafael Mendes. Observers: Aisha Bello, Sergio Costa. Release coord: Connor O’Brien. Routing: Mina Haddad. Infra/DNS: Victor Alvarez. Capacity: Harish Reddy.

Connor O'Brien: confirming we’re inside the approved window + change ticket is green. Feature flag `failover_orchestrator_prod` is currently OFF in prod. Rollback plan: flip flag OFF + revert routing policy change. (reaction: :white_check_mark: x2)

Miles Thornton: quick reminder of stop conditions from the checklist:
- canary error rate > 0.8% for 5m OR p99 latency +40% vs baseline for 5m
- any elevated auth/tokenization errors (usually means config mismatch)
- target region headroom < 20% on the relevant GPU pools

Aisha Bello: dashboards to watch:
- Region health + state machine: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/failover-overview
- Customer impact by tier: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/failover-customer-impact
- SLO burn (multi-window): https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/slo-burn-mr
Baseline right now: us-west p95 420ms, p99 980ms, 5xx 0.06%. us-east similar.

Harish Reddy: capacity check: us-east gpu_pool `hosted-a100-80g` headroom 34% (alloc), queue depth stable. `hosted-h100` headroom 28%. If we push beyond 10% canary we might pinch on a100 depending on batch mix.

Mina Haddad: routing policy ready. We’re not touching DNS today; doing internal routing policy shift only (progressive failover path). Policy diff is scoped to:
- service: inference-gateway
- route: chat.completions
- tier: dev,startup
- region preference: us-west -> us-east (canary percentage)

Victor Alvarez: +1 no DNS. Edge config unchanged. Network probes look clean (packet loss <0.2% on both).

Sergio Costa: alerting is set to page only if we cross stop conditions; otherwise it’ll just annotate dashboards. I’ll drop updates every few mins.

Rafael Mendes: go/no-go check: everyone comfortable proceeding to 1% canary? If any objections speak now.

Allison Grant: no objections. Please make sure the orchestrator audit log is capturing state transitions + who toggled the policy. We’ll need it for the write-up.

Connor O'Brien: good to proceed. I’ll capture timestamps for the change log.

Miles Thornton: proceed. Please start in monitor-only for 2 mins after enabling flag just to confirm ingestion + state machine ticks.

Rafael Mendes: doing it.

Connor O'Brien: flipping feature flag `failover_orchestrator_prod` to ON (monitor-only=true) for hosted inference-gateway. Change ref: REL-FF-219.

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: `failover_orchestrator_prod` -> enabled (monitor-only=true) in env=prod. Actor: connor.obrien. Audit: https://console.redwood.dev/admin/flags/audit?id=REL-FF-219

Miles Thornton: seeing orchestrator heartbeat in metrics. No state transitions (expected).

Aisha Bello: signals look sane. No unexpected gaps in region health ingestion.

Rafael Mendes: ok, moving monitor-only=false + applying 1% canary routing to us-east for scope above.

Mina Haddad: applying routing policy update (1% canary) now. Hold-down timers remain default (15m) but since this is manual action, we’re just exercising the orchestration hooks.

deploy-bot: Routing policy updated: `policy/inference-gateway/progressive-failover` version=1842. Scope: route=chat.completions tiers=[dev,startup]. canary=1%. Actor: mina.haddad. Diff: https://git.redwood.dev/routing/policies/compare/1841..1842

Sergio Costa: annotation posted on dashboards “Canary 1% -> us-east”. Watching p99 and 5xx.

Aisha Bello: first few mins: us-east p95 ticked up ~5% (within noise). Error rate unchanged. Streaming disconnects stable.

Vikram Singh: confirming data plane sees new policy. No unusual cache miss spikes.

Miles Thornton: check token/sec throughput? Sometimes we see micro-bursts at shift.

Sergio Costa: throughput steady. No queue depth change.

Rafael Mendes: hold at 1% for 10 mins per plan. If stable, ramp to 5% then 10%.

Victor Alvarez: network path from edge -> us-east looks normal. No BGP events.

Harish Reddy: capacity still good. headroom now 31% (expected fluctuation).

Aisha Bello: 10-min mark: error rate 0.07% (flat). p99 us-east 1.02s vs baseline 0.99s. All good.

Rafael Mendes: ok moving to 5% canary.

Mina Haddad: updating policy canary=5%.

deploy-bot: Routing policy updated: `policy/inference-gateway/progressive-failover` version=1843. canary=5%. Actor: mina.haddad. Diff: https://git.redwood.dev/routing/policies/compare/1842..1843

Sergio Costa: seeing traffic shift. p95 us-east +8%, still under thresholds. 5xx stable.

Miles Thornton: any auth errors? That’s our canary for config mismatch.

Aisha Bello: auth/tokenization errors unchanged (good). No spike in “model_not_found” either.

Connor O'Brien: reminder: if we hit abort, we revert policy version + flip flag OFF. No other changes needed.

Rafael Mendes: thanks. Holding 5% for 10 mins.

Sergio Costa: small bump in tail (p99 1.12s) for ~2 mins, then back to 1.03s. No correlated 5xx increase. Might be batching warm-up.

Harish Reddy: us-east queue depth briefly rose (p95 queue wait 18ms -> 41ms) but back down.

Miles Thornton: ok. If it doesn’t recur at 10% we’re fine.

Aisha Bello: burn-rate panels look flat; no material SLO impact.

Rafael Mendes: proceeding to 10% canary.

Mina Haddad: applying canary=10%.

deploy-bot: Routing policy updated: `policy/inference-gateway/progressive-failover` version=1844. canary=10%. Actor: mina.haddad. Diff: https://git.redwood.dev/routing/policies/compare/1843..1844

incident-bot: Reminder: stop conditions: 5xx > 0.8% (5m), p99 +40% (5m), capacity headroom < 20%, auth/tokenization anomalies.

Sergio Costa: 10% shift visible. us-east p95 455ms (baseline 430), p99 1.09s. 5xx 0.08%. No pages.

Victor Alvarez: probes still clean.

Vikram Singh: data plane stable. No elevated retries.

Miles Thornton: nice. Let’s hold at 10% for 15 mins then fail back to normal and confirm recovery.

Rafael Mendes: agreed. Holding.

Aisha Bello: customer impact by tier: no obvious regression. Startup tier has slight increase in “timeout_handled_by_client” but it’s within normal band.

Sergio Costa: I’ll clip graphs for the retro.

Harish Reddy: headroom 26% now. Still above limit.

Rafael Mendes: ok. At +15 mins, we’ll revert canary to 0% and disable the flag (monitor-only) after we confirm steady state.

Mina Haddad: ready when you are.

Rafael Mendes: revert canary to 0% now.

Mina Haddad: reverting policy to canary=0% (back to region preference us-west).

deploy-bot: Routing policy updated: `policy/inference-gateway/progressive-failover` version=1845. canary=0%. Actor: mina.haddad. Diff: https://git.redwood.dev/routing/policies/compare/1844..1845

Sergio Costa: traffic shifting back. tails returning to baseline.

Aisha Bello: confirming: p95 us-west 425ms, p99 0.97s; 5xx 0.06%. No lingering elevated disconnects.

Miles Thornton: good. Now flip the feature flag back to OFF (or monitor-only) per plan.

Connor O'Brien: setting `failover_orchestrator_prod` -> enabled (monitor-only=true) for 5 mins while we sanity check audit logs, then OFF.

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: `failover_orchestrator_prod` -> enabled (monitor-only=true) in env=prod. Actor: connor.obrien. Audit: https://console.redwood.dev/admin/flags/audit?id=REL-FF-220

Allison Grant: can someone paste the audit log link for the state machine transitions (even if “none”)?

Miles Thornton: audit trail here: https://console.redwood.dev/admin/failover/audit?window=1713984300-1713991200
We should see policy changes + orchestrator evaluations. No automatic transitions occurred (expected; this was manual progressive test).

Rafael Mendes: looks good. Any final checks before we close out?

Sergio Costa: all metrics back to baseline. No alert noise. The only thing: brief p99 bump at 5% stage; recommend note it + maybe pre-warm batching on target region before ramp.

Aisha Bello: +1. Also the “startup tier timeout handled by client” panel might need a better label; it’s not actionable as-is.

Harish Reddy: capacity returned to normal; no sustained queue increase.

Victor Alvarez: nothing from networking side.

Connor O'Brien: flipping flag OFF now.

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: `failover_orchestrator_prod` -> disabled in env=prod. Actor: connor.obrien. Audit: https://console.redwood.dev/admin/flags/audit?id=REL-FF-221

Rafael Mendes: controlled failover test complete. Summary:
- 1% -> 5% -> 10% progressive shift us-west -> us-east for low-risk scope
- no stop conditions triggered
- minor transient tail bump at 5% but within limits
Next: capture notes in retro doc + file follow-ups for pre-warm + dashboard label.

incident-bot: Incident marked resolved by Rafael Mendes. Duration: 1h 57m. Tags: controlled-test, failover, progressive-routing. Post-test write-up template: https://drive.redwood.dev/sre/post-test-analysis-template
